questions.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Rights?
questions.x: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Constitution (Articles 12–35).

questions.q: The concept of 'Basic Structure' of the Indian Constitution was first introduced by the Supreme Court in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
questions.x: The **Golaknath case (1967)** first recognized judicial review of constitutional amendments, but the **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)** solidified the 'Basic Structure' doctrine.

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the list of recognized official languages?
questions.x: **Schedule 8** lists the 22 scheduled languages (e.g., Hindi, Bengali, Tamil).

questions.q: The term 'Federalism' in the Indian Constitution is best described by which feature?
o: Division of Powers between Centre and States
questions.x: Federalism is defined by the **division of legislative powers** (Union List, State List, Concurrent List) in **Article 246**.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment introduced the concept of 'Anti-Defection Law'?
questions.x: **52nd Amendment (1985)** inserted the Tenth Schedule** to penalize defection from political parties.

questions.q: Which of these rivers flows through the Grand Canyon in the USA?
questions.x: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.

questions.q: The world's largest desert, the Sahara, is located in which continent?
questions.x: The Sahara covers most of North Africa, spanning 11 countries.

questions.q: Which of these is the longest river in the world?
questions.x: The Nile is traditionally considered the longest at ~6,650 km (though some studies suggest the Amazon may be slightly longer).

questions.q: The 'Andes' mountain range is primarily located in which continent?
questions.x: The Andes stretch along the western edge of South America, covering seven countries.

questions.q: The 'Great Barrier Reef' is located off the coast of which country?
questions.x: The Great Barrier Reef lies off Queensland, Australia, and is the world's largest coral reef system.

questions.q: The 'Panama Canal' connects which two oceans?
questions.x: The canal links the Atlantic Ocean (via Caribbean Sea) to the Pacific Ocean, saving ships thousands of miles.
